A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRIMUS datasets and cybersecurity LLM training study. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite appendix insertions and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original training, benchmark, ablation, calibration and safety results, including Tables 5–14 and the appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds a dataset-overlap analysis and a qualitative model-response comparison.

M1.justification: Section 2.2.3 removes Claude 3.5 Sonnet from the randomly selected seed-text rewriting models, retaining GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct and DBRX. This revises the stated augmentation procedure; the model architecture and multi-stage training pipeline remain unchanged.

E1.justification: New Appendix F adds a free-response scenario by removing the answer choices from one CTI-MCQ question about unauthorized browser extensions. This changes the answering task requirements for that case; the training corpora and established benchmark coverage are otherwise retained.

E2.justification: The existing comparator sets remain unchanged, including DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B in Table 7 and ZySec-AI/SecurityLLM and both HackMentor variants in Table 14. Appendix F reuses the existing Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct baseline.

E3.justification: v3 adds an overlap-check protocol using N-grams of lengths 8–13 and a one-question free-response comparison. Appendix C corrects the Nemotron-CC filtering bound from 0.175 to 0.0175, matching the unchanged token-count table. Figure 11 now tells the judge to expect a reference answer. These reported setting changes do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: FAQ Q9 and new Table 15 add a targeted PRIMUS-REASONING/CISSP contamination check, including manual inspection of overlaps. Appendix F adds a single model-output case study. Existing deduplication, dataset-combination, merging, calibration and safety analyses are retained.

E5.justification: No repeated-evaluation counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are added or revised. The new overlap counts are descriptive results rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing dataset statistics and evaluation scores are unchanged, including Tables 5–14 and the relocated Nemotron-CC and Garak tables. New Table 15 reports zero overlaps for N=9–13 and five for N=8. Appendix F adds responses in which Primus names T1176 while Llama supplies broader controls, including a web application firewall.

T1.justification: The existing task definitions, merging-ratio expression and metric explanations are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same dataset and model contributions, novelty scope, and headline gains of 15.9% for continued pretraining and 15.8% on CISSP. The appendix additions support the existing contribution claims.

C2.justification: FAQ Q9 newly interprets the short overlaps as generic question stems and considers potential leakage negligible. Appendix F interprets Primus's response as showing stronger MITRE-framework recall than Llama's broader recommendations. The previously stated model-scale and reinforcement-learning limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Tables 16–17 newly document dataset fields, timestamp conventions and original-source licensing obligations. Filtering and augmentation details are corrected or revised. Figure 11 now mentions a reference answer without providing a corresponding input field, leaving that detail unclear; hardware and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Brown et al. (2020), Language Models are Few-Shot Learners, to support the N-gram decontamination approach in FAQ Q9. The broader positioning relative to cybersecurity pretraining, instruction tuning and reasoning research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The FAQ expands from six to nine questions, and Dataset Details and Sample Outputs appendices are inserted. Subsequent appendix letters and cross-references are updated. Main-section organization and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds three tables for overlap results and dataset schemas. Former Tables 15–17 become Tables 18–20, with appendix reflow, updated prompt panels in Figures 11 and 13, and page-number footers. Existing scientific plots and benchmark-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Dataset schemas and source-use guidance improve usability, and the corrected Nemotron-CC threshold resolves a prose/table inconsistency. The new CISSP overlap check supplies targeted validation absent from v2. These gains are limited: the response comparison covers one question, and Figure 11 introduces an unspecified reference-answer input. Overall, documentation and evidential support improve modestly while the core experimental results remain unchanged.
